hook: On October 4, 2026, Earth slipped directly between the Sun and Saturn.

sections.voiceover: On October 4, 2026, Earth slipped directly between the Sun and Saturn.
sections.visual_cue: Space animation showing Earth, Sun, and Saturn aligning in their orbits.
b_roll: NASA space visualization of planetary alignment

sections.voiceover: This opposition, where Earth aligns between the Sun and Saturn, occurred precisely at 12 UTC. Where did the ringed planet Saturn appear in the sky during this October 2026 event?
sections.visual_cue: Saturn appearing bright against a dark starfield.
b_roll: NASA public domain image of Saturn

sections.voiceover: But Saturn drifted within Cetus, the Whale, making the planet visible throughout the entire night.
sections.visual_cue: Star map highlighting the constellation Cetus.

sections.voiceover: Observers in the United Kingdom tracked Saturn as it reached a peak altitude of 40 degrees. Earth offered the ideal vantage point for viewing this annual opposition of the ringed planet.
sections.visual_cue: Telescopic view of Saturn rising above the horizon.
sections.sfx_cue: Sound of a telescope mount moving smoothly.
b_roll: View of night sky over the UK

sections.voiceover: Watch Saturn in the constellation of Cetus to witness this rare October 4, 2026 alignment.
sections.visual_cue: Slow zoom out from Saturn into the wide starfield.
b_roll: Wide field view of deep space
